meta.title: LLM + RAG Chatbot Documents
meta.description: DDD documentation framework for LLM-powered chatbot projects with RAG grounding over a curated knowledge base, deployed to messaging channels (LINE OA, web chat widget, Messenger, WhatsApp, Telegram). AI reads this file and generates .md files in the correct order with proper cross-references.
meta.applicable_when: Building a conversational AI assistant powered by an LLM with RAG grounding over a curated knowledge base, deployed to one or more messaging channels (LINE OA, web chat widget, Messenger, WhatsApp, Telegram) — distinct from scheduled AI workflows (no real-time conversation) and from web applications (the conversation is the primary UI). Distinct from the context-formalization template: when a knowledge bundle from that template's assembly pipeline is the source of this chatbot's retrieval corpus, its published components enter here as KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md sources, not as a document this template generates.

agent_instructions.role: You are a chatbot documentation generator. Read this file and produce each document listed in phases[], in dependency order.
agent_instructions.generation_order_strategy: Topological sort by depends_on graph. Generate documents with no dependencies first. Each document is the canonical source for its concerns — downstream docs reference upstream docs by document ID. Enum values are defined once in their owner document and only indexed in GLOSSARY.md — downstream documents reference an enum by name, never redefine its values.
agent_instructions.content_language: Write document content in Thai for narrative sections; use English for all identifiers, code, prompt template names, model names, channel API names, and technical terms. Preserve jargon (LLM, RAG, embedding, retrieval, chunk, guardrail, webhook, intent, utterance, containment, groundedness, rich menu, flex message) as English even in Thai sentences.
agent_instructions.quality_gate: Each document must cover all sections[] listed. Validate that cross-references (refs[]) resolve to real document IDs before finishing. Every channel adapter, prompt template, guardrail rule, and knowledge source must be documented exactly once in its canonical doc and referenced elsewhere — no duplicate definitions. Never hardcode company or product names — use placeholders so the template stays reusable. Every enum is defined in exactly one owner document and only indexed in GLOSSARY.md's Enumeration Registry — other documents reference it, never redefine it. Never invent a default for a value that needs calibration (retrieval top-k, similarity threshold, rerank cutoff, temperature, latency budget, retention period) — declare it null with its calibration source instead.
domain_specific_notes: Chatbot ≠ Web App. The conversation IS the UI. CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md replaces UI_SPEC.md and also owns bot persona/tone and escalation flows.

ARCHITECTURE.md describes the message pipeline (channel adapter → session/context → retrieval → LLM → guardrails → render) and includes a Key Architecture Decisions section — there is no separate ADR document.

KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md is the single source of truth for the RAG corpus AND retrieval behavior — sources, ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, reranking, and citation policy all live there.

CHANNEL_INTEGRATION.md stays channel-agnostic at the core via the canonical message envelope defined in DATA_CONTRACTS.md, with per-channel adapter specs (LINE OA, web widget, Messenger, WhatsApp, Telegram).
GUARDRAILS.md is the safety canon — content policy, prompt injection defense, moderation, and grounded-answer enforcement. Never weaken a guardrail without an explicit decision record.

Human handoff spans four documents: triggers/flows in CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md, transport per channel in CHANNEL_INTEGRATION.md, context payload in DATA_CONTRACTS.md, and human-agent operations in RUNBOOK.md.

EVALUATION.md covers offline evals (retrieval metrics, groundedness, red-team) AND online conversation analytics (containment, CSAT, handoff rate). Cost per conversation is tracked in DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md.

Containment ≠ deflection ≠ resolution — a bot that ends the conversation without solving anything scores well on containment but badly on the business goal. EVALUATION.md owns the KPI definitions; GLOSSARY.md owns the terms so the three are never conflated in a dashboard.

Refusal ≠ no-answer ≠ handoff — three distinct terminal outcomes owned by three documents (GUARDRAILS.md, KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md, CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md respectively). Collapsing them into one 'the bot didn't help' bucket makes the analytics uninterpretable.

Session memory ≠ long-term user memory ≠ KB knowledge — three different stores with three different retention rules and three different PDPA legal bases, owned by DATA_CONTRACTS.md, SECURITY_PRIVACY.md and KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md respectively. Never let one silently stand in for another.

requirement_priority ≠ incident_severity. Both use the P0/P1/P2 symbols, but requirement_priority (owned by CRD.md) scores product requirements while incident_severity (owned by RUNBOOK.md) scores operational incidents — two different scales with two different owners that happen to share symbols. TASKS.md carries no priority scale of its own either; a task inherits its priority from the CRD.md requirement it references.

description.th: ผู้ใช้ปลายทางของ chatbot (end user ต่อ channel), human agent ที่รับ handoff, KB curator และ bot admin

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a PERSONAS.md for an LLM + RAG chatbot. Distinguish four persona classes: (1) End User — who converses with the bot to get answers or complete tasks, profiled per channel (LINE OA users behave differently from web widget visitors), (2) Human Agent — who receives escalated conversations and needs full context, (3) KB Curator — who owns knowledge base content and its freshness, (4) Bot Admin/Operator — who tunes prompts, monitors quality, and manages incidents. For each, document role, technical skill, pain points the chatbot addresses, conversation goals, and interactions that are mission-critical.
agent_hints.input_context: Use project brief and stakeholder interviews. End users may span multiple channels with different expectations of tone and response speed.
agent_hints.validation: Each persona must have: name/role, technical_skill, pain_points[], conversation_goals[], critical_interactions[]. At least one End User persona, one Human Agent persona, and one KB Curator or Bot Admin persona must be defined.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONSTRAINTS.md documenting all fixed constraints the chatbot must operate within. Cover: privacy/compliance (PDPA, what user messages the LLM may see, chat log retention), model availability (which LLM models are accessible, context window), cost ceiling (per conversation, monthly), latency (max seconds per reply per channel — users abandon slow bots), channel/integration constraints (LINE Messaging API limits, webhook timeout, WhatsApp template rules, rate limits), and language coverage (which languages the bot must handle, fallback language).
agent_hints.input_context: Gather from stakeholder interviews, channel platform documentation, vendor SLAs, and corporate IT policy. These are non-negotiable inputs to architecture and conversation design.
agent_hints.validation: Must address all six constraint categories. Each constraint must be stated as a clear, testable requirement (e.g., 'p95 reply latency must not exceed 5 seconds on web widget').

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a VPD.md using the Value Proposition Canvas adapted for chatbots. Customer = End User persona (primary) and the business operating the bot (secondary). Jobs = questions answered and tasks completed through conversation. Pain = friction in the current support/answer path (queue time, unfindable FAQs, limited service hours). Gain = instant answers, 24/7 availability, consistent quality. Pain Relievers and Gain Creators are produced by the bot's capabilities (RAG-grounded answers, guided flows, seamless human handoff). e.g., Pain: 'user waits 20 minutes in chat queue', Gain: 'answer in under 10 seconds any time of day', Pain Reliever: 'RAG answer with citation from the latest policy document'.
agent_hints.input_context: Depends on personas document for end-user profiles and constraints document for what the bot can feasibly deliver (latency, languages, channels).
agent_hints.validation: Must contain at least one entry for each of: customer_jobs, pains, gains, pain_relievers, gain_creators, value_propositions. Each pain reliever must link back to a pain; each gain creator must link to a gain.

description.en: PRD-equivalent for chatbots — defines use cases and in-scope intents, out-of-scope items, channels and languages, functional/non-functional requirements, and KPIs.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CRD.md (Chatbot Requirements Document). Write a clear problem statement, define measurable success metrics (containment rate, CSAT, first-response accuracy, handoff rate), enumerate use cases as in-scope intents in 'When a user asks [intent], the bot [does action], so that [user gets value]' format, explicitly list out-of-scope intents with rationale and the fallback behavior when users ask them, declare launch channels and supported languages, categorize functional requirements as P0/P1/P2, specify NFRs (per-reply latency, cost per conversation, availability), and map cut capabilities to future phases.
agent_hints.input_context: Reference personas, vpd, and constraints. Every use case must map to an End User persona and at least one conversation goal in PERSONAS.md. Scope must fit within CONSTRAINTS.md.
agent_hints.validation: Every functional requirement must have a priority and an acceptance criterion. Every use case must reference a persona. Every out-of-scope intent must state the fallback behavior. Every NFR must have a measurable threshold.

description.en: The chatbot's ubiquitous language — agreed business and conversation/RAG term definitions; the naming authority for intent names, KB metadata, and prompt variables.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a GLOSSARY.md defining the chatbot's ubiquitous language. Collect every business term used by personas and in CRD.md use cases, plus chatbot/RAG technical terms the team must share (intent, utterance, containment, deflection, resolution, escalation, groundedness, chunk, citation, session). Give each term one agreed definition, its owner role, and synonyms that must NOT appear in intent names, schema fields, or prompt variables. Map every term to where it is implemented: an intent name in CRD.md, a KB metadata field or taxonomy value in DATA_CONTRACTS.md, or a prompt variable in PROMPT_SPEC.md. Record disputed terms with the competing definitions and the resolution. Intent classification and eval labeling quality depend on these definitions being unambiguous.
agent_hints.input_context: Terms originate from PERSONAS.md profiles and CRD.md use cases. Every intent name and classification label used downstream must trace back to a term defined here. The Enumeration Registry section is the single index of every enum used across the project, and it has two kinds of row. These exist in every project built from this template: intent and requirement_priority (CRD.md), work_item_status (TASKS.md), escalation_trigger (CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md), prompt_id (PROMPT_SPEC.md), guardrail_rule_id and prohibited_topic_class (GUARDRAILS.md), event_type, content_part_type, handoff_state and pii_classification (DATA_CONTRACTS.md), channel (CHANNEL_INTEGRATION.md), KPI metric names (EVALUATION.md) and incident_severity (RUNBOOK.md). On top of those, register every domain enum this project's own documents own — the template cannot name them in advance because they come from the business the bot serves, so the registry is always longer than this list and its length differs per project. Note that requirement_priority and incident_severity share the symbols P0/P1/P2 while being different scales with different owners; the registry keeps them apart by name. This document indexes; it never redefines a value already owned elsewhere.
agent_hints.validation: Every term must have exactly one definition and one owner role. Every intent name must map to a term. Disputed terms must record the resolution. No orphan terms that map to nothing. The Enumeration Registry must map every enum listed in input_context, plus every domain enum any document in this set owns, to exactly one owner document and contain zero enum values. Walk it in both directions — from each registry row to the owner document that declares the values, and from every enum the documents actually use back to a registry row.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md — the conversation is the product's UI, so this document plays the role UI_SPEC.md plays in a web app. Define the bot persona (name, personality, tone of voice per language, what it never says) with sample utterances. Model every in-scope intent from CRD.md with example utterances and entities to extract. Design dialog flows per use case (happy path + edge branches) in Mermaid or numbered-turn format. Specify multi-turn context rules (what the bot remembers within a session, slot filling, topic switching). Design fallback and repair: what happens on low-confidence understanding, no KB answer, or repeated failure. Design escalation flows: triggers (user asks for human, sentiment, N failed attempts, sensitive topic), what the user sees during handoff, and behavior outside agent hours. Specify rich message usage (quick replies, carousels, rich menu) with a text-only degradation for every rich element. Define localization rules per supported language.
agent_hints.input_context: Every in-scope intent in CRD.md must have a dialog flow or be explicitly grouped into one. Persona tone must fit the End User personas in PERSONAS.md. The persona and tone defined here are the single source for PROMPT_SPEC.md's system persona prompt. Escalation triggers follow the escalation term in GLOSSARY.md — the same definition behind the handoff rate KPI and the escalation_trigger enum in DATA_CONTRACTS.md.
agent_hints.validation: Every in-scope intent from CRD.md must appear in exactly one dialog flow. Bot persona must include at least 3 do/don't utterance pairs. Every escalation trigger must define the user-facing message. Every rich message element must have a text-only degradation.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an ARCHITECTURE.md for the chatbot. Begin with a Mermaid diagram of the end-to-end message pipeline: channel adapter (webhook in) → session/context loader → understanding (intent/language) → retrieval (RAG) → LLM generation → guardrails check → response render → channel adapter (send out). Document each stage with responsibility, inputs, outputs, and the model weakness it compensates for. Document session/context management (store, TTL, concurrent messages from the same user). State which model is used at each stage and why (cheap model for intent/language detection, strong model for grounded generation). Profile latency per stage against the per-reply budget in CONSTRAINTS.md and describe scaling for concurrent conversations. List failure modes (LLM timeout, retrieval empty, channel webhook retry storms, session store down) each with detection signal and mitigation. agent_hints.instruction: Generate a KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md — the canonical RAG document. Define the index and its metadata schema (source ID, section, language, effective date, audience) used for filtering. Specify retrieval behavior: top-k, similarity threshold, metadata filters per intent, reranking model and cutoff, and the query rewriting step for multi-turn questions. Define the citation policy (every factual answer cites source IDs) and the no-answer policy (below-threshold retrieval → honest no-answer response per CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md, never fabricate). Define freshness: re-ingestion schedule, corpus versioning, and stale-content detection. Map in-scope intents from CRD.md to sources and record known coverage gaps.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a GUARDRAILS.md — the safety canon for a user-facing bot exposed to adversarial input. Define the content policy: prohibited topics the bot never engages (from CRD.md out-of-scope plus universal categories like legal/medical advice, competitor disparagement, personal data of others), each with the refusal behavior. Document prompt injection and jailbreak defense: at least 3 attack vectors (instruction override in user message, injection embedded in KB content, multi-turn gradual jailbreak) with mitigations (input isolation delimiters from PROMPT_SPEC.md, instruction hierarchy, output checks). Define grounded-answer enforcement: how the pipeline verifies factual answers cite retrieved chunks per KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md, and what happens on failure (regenerate, degrade to no-answer). Document the moderation pipeline: pre-LLM input checks and post-LLM output checks, ordering, latency budget, and block behavior. Define refusal and disclaimer style consistent with the persona in CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md — refusals stay polite and offer an alternative (rephrase or handoff). Establish guardrail change control: every rule change needs an owner, a red-team re-run, and a version bump.
agent_hints.input_context: Prohibited topics extend CRD.md out-of-scope items. Refusal tone must match CONVERSATION_DESIGN.md persona. Injection defenses coordinate with PROMPT_SPEC.md input isolation and are verified by EVALUATION.md red-team suites. Grounded-answer enforcement applies the groundedness definition from GLOSSARY.md — the same term that labels the golden dataset. Read references/owasp-llm01-indirect-injection.md for the indirect prompt injection threat model — the 'injection embedded in KB content' vector is exactly the case that reference documents; map its mitigations to specific GUARD-NNN rule IDs rather than restating them generically.
agent_hints.validation: Every prohibited topic must have a defined refusal behavior. Injection defense must cover at least 3 attack vectors with mitigations. Grounded-answer enforcement must define the failure action. Every guardrail rule must have an ID and an owner. Each of the three injection/jailbreak attack vectors must name at least one mitigation and one detection signal, not mitigation alone.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an AGENTS.md (also valid as CLAUDE.md) for the chatbot project. Provide a brief overview (what the bot does, channels, KB domain). List the exact tech stack: LLM models per pipeline stage, embedding model, vector store, session store, channel SDKs — all version-pinned. Document coding conventions: adapter structure per channel, envelope handling, naming for intents and prompts (PROMPT-NNN, GUARD-NNN). State prompt and guardrail change rules: never edit a prompt without bumping its version in PROMPT_SPEC.md and re-running eval; never weaken a guardrail without the GUARDRAILS.md change-control process. List forbidden patterns: hardcoded secrets or channel tokens, inline prompts outside PROMPT_SPEC.md, bypassing the canonical envelope with channel-specific logic in the core pipeline, disabling moderation checks in production, answering factual questions without retrieval. Define minimum evaluation requirements per release. State PDPA/PII rules referencing the strip/mask lists in SECURITY_PRIVACY.md and DATA_CONTRACTS.md classifications. Every forbidden pattern must pair the prohibition with its correct alternative — never list a prohibition alone.

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md combining deployment and operations. Document dev/staging/production environments — staging uses sandbox channel accounts and a staging KB index; production uses live channel accounts. Document the deployment procedure (build, deploy behind health check, verify webhook reachability, smoke-test one conversation per channel before routing traffic). Document channel registration per CHANNEL_INTEGRATION.md: webhook URL configuration, signature secrets, and how to verify each channel is receiving events. Document KB operations: index deployment, the scheduled refresh job per KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md, corpus version promotion, and re-index procedure. List every secret with setup steps (placeholder values only). Specify cost monitoring: cost per conversation (LLM + embedding + reranking), daily dashboards, alert thresholds, budget guardrails against conversation-volume spikes. Document the kill switch — how to take the bot offline per channel immediately (auto-reply maintenance message, route all traffic to human/ticket) — and rollback for code, prompt versions, KB corpus versions, and guardrail set versions independently (guardrail versions follow GUARDRAILS.md change control), matching the four change axes in CHANGELOG.md. Define health checks (webhook liveness per channel, LLM API reachability, vector store latency, session store health).

agent_hints.instruction: Generate an EVALUATION.md covering both offline evaluation and online conversation analytics. Offline: define the eval strategy (per-prompt change, per-KB-corpus change, per-release, continuous production sampling). Document the golden conversation dataset — curated multi-turn conversations with expected outcomes per in-scope intent from CRD.md, including edge cases (typos, mixed language, topic switches). Specify retrieval evaluation: a query→relevant-chunks eval set with recall@k, MRR, and precision thresholds — retrieval quality bounds answer quality. Define groundedness and citation tests (every factual claim traces to a retrieved chunk; citation accuracy threshold). Define the safety red-team suite covering GUARDRAILS.md attack vectors (injection, jailbreak, prohibited topics) with pass criteria. Define prompt regression: any prompt version bump per PROMPT_SPEC.md re-runs the affected golden set and blocks promotion on regression. Online: define the conversation analytics built on the event schema in DATA_CONTRACTS.md — KPIs (containment rate, CSAT, handoff rate, no-answer rate, avg turns to resolution) each with definition, formula, target, and dashboard. Define the feedback loop: user feedback and human-agent corrections feed new golden cases and KB gap reports.

Read references/noisy-evaluation-and-budget.md for why LLM-judge groundedness scoring is a noisy evaluator (Ū = U + ε), repeated evaluation and minimum-meaningful-difference before calling a prompt change a regression. items.text_th: Containment ≠ Deflection ≠ Resolution — containment วัดว่า bot จบบทสนทนาโดยไม่ escalate ไป human (นับได้ง่ายแต่ตีความผิดง่าย); deflection วัดว่า bot กันไม่ให้ผู้ใช้ติดต่อ human เลย (business goal ของบางองค์กร); resolution วัดว่าปัญหาของผู้ใช้ถูกแก้จริง (สิ่งที่ผู้ใช้แคร์) — bot ที่ contain สูงแต่ resolve ต่ำคือ false positive ของความสำเร็จ ต้องแยก metric ทั้งสามใน dashboard เสมอ ดู GLOSSARY.md สำหรับนิยาม
items.text_en: Containment ≠ Deflection ≠ Resolution — containment measures whether the bot ends the conversation without escalating to a human (easy to count, easy to misread); deflection measures whether the bot prevents the user from reaching a human at all (an org's business goal); resolution measures whether the user's problem was actually solved (what the user cares about) — a bot with high containment and low resolution is a false positive for success; the three metrics must stay visually separate on the dashboard, see GLOSSARY.md for the definitions

items.text_th: KPI Definitions — containment rate, deflection rate (บทสนทนาที่ user ไม่พยายามติดต่อ human เลย / ทั้งหมด), resolution rate (บทสนทนาที่ user รายงานหรือ CSAT ยืนยันว่าปัญหาถูกแก้จริง / ทั้งหมด), CSAT, handoff rate, no-answer rate, avg turns to resolution — แต่ละตัวมี formula จาก event schema

agent_hints.instruction: Generate a README.md. Include a one-paragraph description of what the bot does, its channels, and the KB domain. Provide a quick-start aimed at operators — how to verify the bot is alive on each channel, where to see logs and dashboards, how to trigger the kill switch. List prerequisites (LLM API key, channel accounts, vector store, agent console). Provide activation steps for a fresh deployment referencing DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md. Describe daily usage (what end users see per channel, how feedback works, how agents take over). Brief architecture overview with a link to ARCHITECTURE.md. Contributing guidelines (how to propose a prompt change through the PROMPT_SPEC.md version + eval gate, how to add a KB source, how to add a channel). License.
agent_hints.input_context: Use CRD.md for the bot description and scope, ARCHITECTURE.md for the architecture overview, DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md for activation steps, EVALUATION.md for dashboards.
agent_hints.validation: Must include a working quick-start an operator can follow on day one to verify the bot is healthy on every channel. Must link to all canonical documents (ARCHITECTURE.md, KNOWLEDGE_BASE.md, PROMPT_SPEC.md, GUARDRAILS.md, RUNBOOK.md). Activation steps must be testable without production data.
